title: Black body radiation
examTip: Know that all bodies emit and absorb infrared radiation, whatever their temperature. Know what a perfect black body is. Be ready to explain a body's temperature using the balance between radiation absorbed and radiation emitted.
introTips: Every object emits and absorbs infrared radiation, even a cold one.
A perfect black body absorbs all the radiation that hits it. It is also the best possible emitter.
If a body absorbs radiation faster than it emits it, its temperature goes up.
intro: Everything around you is giving out infrared radiation, including you. In this lesson you learn how the radiation a body emits depends on its temperature. You learn what a perfect black body is. You also learn how the balance of radiation in and out sets the temperature of an object, and of the Earth.

keyPoints.heading: All bodies emit and absorb infrared radiation
keyPoints.content: All bodies (objects) emit and absorb infrared radiation. This is true whatever their temperature. Even ice emits infrared radiation. The hotter the body, the more infrared radiation it radiates in a given time. The intensity and the wavelength distribution of the radiation depend on the temperature of the body. - A hotter body emits radiation with a greater intensity. - A hotter body emits more of its radiation at shorter wavelengths. This is why a piece of metal glows red, then yellow-white, as it gets hotter.
writeBullets: All bodies emit and absorb infrared radiation, whatever their temperature
Hotter body → more infrared radiation radiated in a given time
Intensity and wavelength distribution of the emission depend on temperature
Hotter body → greater intensity, more radiation at shorter wavelengths

keyTerms.def: Electromagnetic radiation that all bodies emit and absorb; hotter bodies radiate more of it in a given time
How much radiation energy arrives or is emitted per second, for each unit of area

keyPoints.memTip: Everything glows in infrared. Hotter = more, and shorter wavelengths.
keyPoints.tutor_note: A common wrong idea is that only hot objects emit radiation. Ask the student whether an ice cube emits infrared radiation.

keyPoints.heading: Perfect black bodies
keyPoints.content: A perfect black body is an object that absorbs all of the radiation incident on it (all the radiation that hits it). A black body does not reflect any radiation. It does not transmit any radiation either. A good absorber is also a good emitter. So a perfect black body would be the best possible emitter of radiation.
writeBullets: Perfect black body: absorbs all the radiation incident on it
Does not reflect or transmit any radiation
A good absorber is also a good emitter
So a perfect black body is the best possible emitter

keyTerms.def: An object that absorbs all of the radiation incident on it; it reflects and transmits none, and is the best possible emitter

keyPoints.memTip: Black body: absorbs ALL, reflects none, transmits none, emits best.
keyPoints.tutor_note: Students may think a black body cannot emit because it absorbs everything. Stress that a good absorber is also a good emitter.

keyPoints.heading: Temperature and the balance of radiation
keyPoints.content: A body at constant temperature absorbs radiation at the same rate as it emits radiation. - If a body absorbs radiation faster than it emits radiation, its temperature increases. - If a body emits radiation faster than it absorbs radiation, its temperature decreases. Everyday example: a hot drink in a room emits radiation faster than it absorbs it. So it cools down. When it reaches room temperature, the two rates are equal. Its temperature then stays the same. The Earth: the temperature of the Earth depends on many factors. These include the rates of absorption and emission of radiation. They also include the reflection of radiation into space. - Radiation from the Sun reaches the Earth. Some is reflected back into space, by clouds and the ground. - The rest is absorbed. It warms the Earth's surface and atmosphere. - The Earth's surface and atmosphere emit infrared radiation. Some of it goes back into space. If the Earth absorbs radiation at the same rate as it emits it, its temperature stays constant.
writeBullets: Constant temperature: absorbing radiation at the same rate as emitting it
Absorbs faster than it emits → temperature increases
Emits faster than it absorbs → temperature decreases
Earth's temperature depends on rates of absorption and emission, and on reflection of radiation into space
Some of the Sun's radiation is reflected into space; the rest warms the surface and atmosphere
Earth's surface and atmosphere emit infrared radiation back towards space

keyTerms.def: The state of a body that absorbs radiation at the same rate as it emits radiation

keyPoints.memTip: In faster than out = warms up. Out faster than in = cools down. Equal = steady.
keyPoints.tutor_note: Use the hot drink example first. Then ask the student to apply the same idea to the Earth.

0.question: Which statement about infrared radiation is correct?
options: Only hot objects emit infrared radiation
All bodies emit and absorb infrared radiation, whatever their temperature
Cold objects absorb infrared radiation but never emit it
Hotter objects emit less infrared radiation in a given time
0.correctFeedback: Correct. All bodies emit and absorb infrared radiation. The hotter the body, the more it radiates in a given time.
0.wrongFeedback: All bodies emit and absorb infrared radiation, whatever their temperature. Hotter bodies radiate more in a given time.

1.question: What is a perfect black body?
options: An object that reflects all the radiation that hits it
An object that emits no radiation
An object that absorbs all of the radiation incident on it
An object that transmits all radiation
1.correctFeedback: Correct. A perfect black body absorbs all the radiation incident on it. It is also the best possible emitter.
1.wrongFeedback: A perfect black body absorbs all of the radiation incident on it. It reflects and transmits none. It is the best possible emitter.

2.question: An object absorbs radiation faster than it emits radiation. What happens to its temperature?
2.correctFeedback: Correct. More radiation is absorbed than emitted each second, so the temperature increases.
2.wrongFeedback: If a body absorbs radiation faster than it emits it, its temperature increases. It stays constant only when the two rates are equal.

commonMistakes: Saying only hot objects emit radiation. All bodies emit infrared radiation, whatever their temperature.
Saying a black body emits nothing because it absorbs everything. A perfect black body is the best possible emitter.
Saying an object at constant temperature has stopped absorbing or emitting. It is doing both at the same rate.
examTips: For a temperature question, compare the rate of absorbing with the rate of emitting. Say which is bigger.
For the Earth, mention absorption, emission and reflection of radiation into space.
When you describe a perfect black body, say it absorbs all the radiation incident on it.
